answer: Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 4 bits per word is rejected before grading, because it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. Because the entropy is measured at the mirror gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the lagoon audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. A farm emitting 80 variations of one paragraph hence pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the copper panel. That is 28 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
